selectedWork.title: How AI helped us uncover Red Bull’s influence on energy drink research

relatedStudies.title: How LLMs perform in breaking news scenarios
relatedStudies.label: Presentation slides

relatedStudies.title: How ChatGPT misrepresents publisher content
relatedStudies.coverageHtml: Covered in TechCrunch, The Verge, and Futurism, among others.

selectedWork.descriptionHtml: We tested eight AI search tools on their ability to identify and cite news articles. We found that more than 60 percent of their responses contained errors, often delivered with unwarranted confidence. The tools misattributed reporting, linked to copied or syndicated versions, and invented URLs.
selectedWork.moreHtml: This report has been covered by Nieman Lab, Ars Technica, Axios, El País, and others.

selectedWork.imageAlt: Annotated photograph of flooding in Valencia showing visual clues used by AI to infer its location
selectedWork.title: Why AI Models Are Bad at Verifying Photos
selectedWork.descriptionHtml: People are increasingly using AI to fact-check images. But these tools can give convincing, misleading answers about whether an image is real and where it came from, contributing to the misinformation. We tested whether AI chatbots could verify news photographs and establish their provenance, and examined how they reasoned through the task.

selectedWork.imageAlt: Animated chart of OpenAI’s lawsuits, deals, and grants involving news publishers
selectedWork.title: AI Deals and Disputes Tracker
selectedWork.description: The relationships between news publishers and AI companies could be difficult to follow. A publisher can license content to one company, sue another, and receive grant funding from a third. We designed a tracker and created visualizations to help readers explore the various relationships between publishers and AI companies.
